notes: One task that shows what the design skill changes. `task agent:eval` (scripts/agenteval) runs it against a fresh `apic demo` project through the Claude Code CLI, once with the apic and api-design skills installed and once with the apic skill alone, so the lift measured is the design knowledge rather than knowing how to run apic. The verify command proves the document with apic itself: `apic import` reads it, and `apic mock` serves it on port 8097 so a probe can ask for the documented 404 and 422 (a `Prefer: code=` header) and for example bodies with the fields the real API has. Ids are unique across every skill's evals file. <dir> in the prompt is the project's path.

evals.name: describe-todos-in-openapi
evals.prompt: The project at <dir> talks to a running todos API with the requests in todos.http, and the apic binary is on PATH. Write an OpenAPI 3.1 document at <dir>/openapi.yaml that describes the five todos operations (list, create, get, update, delete under /todos) as the API actually behaves: probe it with the project's requests rather than guessing, and include everything a client needs to know, the error responses the API really gives as well as the successes. Then prove the document: `apic import openapi.yaml -o <some scratch directory outside the project>` must produce requests that run against the live API, and `apic mock openapi.yaml` must serve realistic responses. Do not use curl and do not add other files to the project.
evals.expected_output: A document with an operationId on each of the five operations, a response schema and an example on each success (the todo has id, title and done; the list is an array), the 401 on every operation, the 404 on get, update and delete, the 422 on create with its fields object, the 400 on a bad done filter, and the X-Total-Count and Link headers on the list; a bearer security scheme applied to all of them; servers pointing at the local API. The agent probes the API with apic run (not-found, create-todo-invalid, list-todos) to see the real shapes, imports into a scratch directory, and runs the imported requests or the mock before answering. It does not read http-client.private.env.json or the session file.

checks.verify:
set -e; test -f openapi.yaml; scratch=$(mktemp -d); trap 'kill $mock 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT; apic import openapi.yaml -o "$scratch/imported" --json >/dev/null; n=$(apic -C "$scratch/imported" list --json | jq '.requests | length'); apic mock openapi.yaml --port 8097 >/dev/null 2>&1 & mock=$!; sleep 1; printf '### documented 404
# @name get-missing
# @assert status == 404
GET http://127.0.0.1:8097/todos/999
Prefer: code=404

### documented 422
# @name create-invalid
# @assert status == 422
POST http://127.0.0.1:8097/todos
Prefer: code=422
Content-Type: application/json

{"title": ""}

### documented 401
# @name list-anonymous
# @assert status == 401
GET http://127.0.0.1:8097/todos
Prefer: code=401

### example todo
# @name get-one
# @assert status == 200
# @assert body.$.id exists
# @assert body.$.title exists
# @assert body.$.done exists
GET http://127.0.0.1:8097/todos/1

### example list
# @name list
# @assert status == 200
# @assert body.$ isArray
GET http://127.0.0.1:8097/todos
' > "$scratch/probe.http"; apic -C "$scratch" run probe.http --json --keep-going | jq -s -c --argjson n "$n" '{imported: $n, enough_operations: ($n >= 5), mock_checks: length, all_documented: all(.ok)}'
